verdict.rationale: The SDK's core mechanic is defining agents (LLM + instructions + tools) and running them via Runner.run()/run_sync()/run_streamed(), which is essentially delegating a task to an AI agent that can use tools, hand off to other specialized agents, and maintain session memory — directly matching 'delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant.' Handoffs and 'agents as tools' further support delegation patterns, and tracing/session memory back the experience with production-ready plumbing.  missing for 10: independent/hands-on end-user validation of the delegation experience (evidence is community commentary comparing complexity, not confirming task-delegation UX), and no example of a non-developer 'AI-native user' actually delegating tasks through a finished product UI (this is a developer SDK, not an end-user-facing assistant).
